summary_paragraph: A 72-year-old woman with a history of liver transplant for HCV cirrhosis, chronic kidney disease, and diabetes was admitted due to a three-week history of non-bloody, mucus-containing diarrhea and dehydration. Her creatinine rose from a baseline of 1.6–2.0 to 2.2, indicating acute on chronic kidney injury, likely pre-renal from fluid loss. She was treated with IV fluids and albumin, leading to improvement in renal function with creatinine decreasing to 1.2 by discharge. Diarrhea resolved during the hospitalization. Stool studies were negative for C. diff, bacterial pathogens, CMV, Giardia, and parasites, though one O&P remained pending. Tacrolimus level was initially elevated at 5.6 but decreased to 3.8 with dose management. Her Lasix and nadolol were held temporarily due to kidney concerns and nadolol was restarted upon improvement. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to follow up with hepatology for pending test results, tacrolimus monitoring, and guidance on restarting Lasix.
problems: HCV cirrhosis c/b HCC s/p liver transplant c/b recurrent HCV, ascites, grade II esophageal varices
